records.title: Connect your agents
records.text: Coding agents read your docs through the MCP server, the .md twin of every page and llms.txt . They write docs through the same tools, and a person signs the changes off.

records.title: Connect your agents
records.heading: The MCP server
records.text: Each doc set has an MCP endpoint. Add it to Claude Code with one command: Terminal $ claude mcp add --transport http larecipe https://larecipe.saleem.dev/docs/mcp

records.title: Connect your agents
records.heading: Skills and hooks
records.text: The installer writes four skills and a pre-push hook. The hook holds a push once when the affected pages were not updated.

records.title: Connect your agents
records.heading: Page actions
records.text: Every page offers Copy as Markdown, View as Markdown and Open in Claude, ChatGPT or Cursor, next to the table of contents.

records.title: Components
records.text: Components are tags in your Markdown. The server renders each one as HTML that works without JavaScript; the browser adds behavior where it helps.

records.title: Components
records.heading: Callouts
records.text: Note A callout gets its meaning from the label, never from a tinted background. Tip Run php artisan larecipe:validate before you push to catch broken links. Important Agent edits made outside a pull request stay drafts until a person publishes them. Warning Verify the signature before you trust a webhook payload. Danger Never put secrets in docs. There is no <Config> component, on purpose.

records.title: Components
records.heading: Steps
records.text: Write the page Add a Markdown file under docs/ . Frontmatter holds page-level settings only. Validate The validator checks links, components and references, and prints JSON for agents. Ship it with the code The docs change rides in the same pull request as the code it describes.

records.heading: Tabs
records.text: Composer Install with Composer and publish nothing: the UI is served from the package. Laravel Cloud Provenance is compiled at build time, because production servers have no git history. Docker Run php artisan larecipe:optimize in your image build, next to route:cache .

records.title: Components
records.heading: Accordion
records.text: Does LaRecipe need Node on my server? No. The UI is built before release and served from the package. Node is only needed on a developer machine if you write your own components. Can I keep docs private? Yes. A doc set can require authentication or a gate, and the same rule applies to search, Markdown and MCP.

records.title: Configuration
records.text: LaRecipe splits configuration in two. Infrastructure routes, the source driver, caching, AI lives in config/larecipe.php . Content and presentation name, theme, versions, navigation live in larecipe.json next to your docs.

records.title: Configuration
records.heading: Doc sets
records.text: One app can serve several doc sets, each with its own route, source and access rules. php 'sets' = 'docs' = 'route' = 'prefix' = 'docs' , 'handbook' = 'route' = 'prefix' = 'handbook' , 'access' = 'mode' = 'auth' , ,

records.title: Configuration
records.heading: Search
records.text: The default driver searches in the browser. The index is built per version, locale and audience, so a private page never reaches a guest's browser.

records.title: Configuration
records.heading: Access
records.text: Set access.mode to public , auth or gate . The same policy applies to every surface: HTML, Markdown, search, llms.txt and MCP.

records.title: Frontmatter
records.text: Frontmatter holds settings for one page. Everything about the doc set lives in larecipe.json .

records.title: Release checklist
records.text: Work through these sections in order. Each one is short; together they keep a release from surprising your readers.

records.title: Release checklist
records.heading: Freeze the scope
records.text: Agree on what ships. Anything that is not merged by the freeze waits for the next release. Write the list down where the team can see it, and link each item to its pull request. A scope that keeps moving is the most common reason docs fall behind. Freezing it gives the docs a fixed target.

records.title: Release checklist
records.heading: Update the docs
records.text: Run the affected-pages check against the release branch. It lists every page whose sources changed since the last tag.

records.title: Release checklist
records.heading: Read the diff
records.text: Read each docs diff next to its code diff. The question is always the same: would a reader who only saw the new page do the right thing?

records.title: Release checklist
records.heading: Check the examples
records.text: Examples should come from real code. Snippet includes fail validation when the region they point at disappears, which is exactly what you want.

records.title: Release checklist
records.heading: Validate
records.text: Run the validator with JSON output in CI. Broken links, unknown components and missing references fail the build instead of reaching a reader. bash php artisan larecipe:validate --json

records.title: Release checklist
records.heading: Check provenance
records.text: Open a few changed pages and read the provenance line. It should name the change that touched the page and the person who approved it.

records.title: Release checklist
records.heading: Search and agents
records.text: Search for the new feature by name. Then fetch the page as Markdown and read it the way an agent will. If the Markdown is confusing, the HTML probably is too.

records.title: Release checklist
records.heading: MCP
records.text: Call the search tool from your coding agent and make sure the new page is in the top results for the obvious query.

records.title: Release checklist
records.heading: Tag the release
records.text: Tag the release from the merge commit. The docs version that matches the tag is the one readers will see by default.

records.title: Release checklist
records.heading: Announce it
records.text: Write the changelog entry in plain words. Say what changed, why, and what a reader has to do, if anything.

records.title: Release checklist
records.heading: After the release
records.text: Watch the zero-result searches for a week. They are the clearest signal of what the docs still do not cover.

records.title: Webhooks
records.text: Webhooks tell your app that something happened elsewhere. Each delivery is signed, so you can prove it came from the sender.

records.title: Webhooks
records.heading: Verify the signature
records.text: Read the raw body, compute the HMAC with your signing secret and compare it in constant time. php $expected = hash hmac 'sha256', $request- getContent , $secret ; abort unless hash equals $expected, $request- header 'X-Signature' , 401 ;

records.title: Webhooks
records.heading: Retries
records.text: Failed deliveries are retried with backoff. Retries carry the same event id, so store the ids you processed and skip repeats.

records.title: Webhooks
records.heading: Testing locally
records.text: Expose your local app with a tunnel and point the sender at it. Keep the signing secret out of the docs; reference the config key instead.

records.title: Introduction
records.text: LaRecipe turns a folder of Markdown inside your Laravel app into a docs site that people and agents can read. Pages are served as HTML for readers, as Markdown for agents, and through an MCP server for coding tools. Demo video coming soon Demo · 2:40

records.text: - Docs in the same repository as the code they describe, reviewed in the same pull request. - A page that says when it changed, what changed it and who approved it. - Search that answers as you type, and Ask for questions the search cannot. - Every page as Markdown at its .md URL, listed in llms.txt . records.title: Introduction
records.heading: How it works
records.text: Your coding agent updates the affected pages before it pushes. A reviewer reads the docs diff next to the code diff. When the pull request merges, the page says so. The loop · each change, reviewed and published

records.title: Installation
records.heading: Requirements
records.text: PHP 8.3+ Laravel 12 or 13 Composer 2 LaRecipe needs no Node.js on your servers. The UI ships prebuilt inside the package.

records.title: Installation
records.heading: Install the package
records.text: Require the package Terminal $ composer require larecipe/larecipe Run the installer It asks where your docs live and which agents you use, then wires everything up. Nothing is written without a preview. Terminal $ php artisan larecipe:install Where should your docs live? › docs/ Connect coding agents? › Claude Code, Codex, Cursor ✓ Wrote docs/larecipe.json ✓ Registered MCP server "larecipe" Connec

records.title: Installation
records.heading: Choose a source
records.text: Docs live in your repository by default. Teams that want an admin UI can keep them in the database instead. Repository Markdown files in docs/ , reviewed in the same pull request as the code. This is the recommended source. Database Pages stored in your database and edited in the admin UI, always served through a cache. Changes made in a pull request travel as docs migrations.

records.title: Installation
records.heading: Configure the route
records.text: The docs answer at /docs by default. Change the prefix in config/larecipe.php : config/larecipe.php 'route' = 'prefix' = 'docs' , 'prefix' = env 'LARECIPE PREFIX' , 'help' , 'middleware' = 'web' , 'auth' , , Warning Private docs must stay behind your own middleware. LaRecipe applies the same access rules to HTML, Markdown, search and MCP, but the route is yours to protect.
